title: Semantic Dissimilarity Guided Locality Preserving Projections for Partial Label Dimensionality Reduction

problem.claim: Partial label learning trains on candidate-label sets containing one ground-truth label, creating a need for dimensionality reduction under weak supervision.

gap.claim: Existing partial label dimensionality reduction methods use disambiguated labels but overlook semantic dissimilarity information contained in labeling confidences.

contributions.claim: SDLPP combines global semantic dissimilarity relationships with local neighborhood information for partial label dimensionality reduction.

SDLPP uses an alternating procedure for candidate-label disambiguation, semantic dissimilarity generation, and dimensionality reduction, with updates based on the previous iteration's low-dimensional data.
SDLPP maps the original data into a pre-specified low-dimensional feature space.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe SDLPP as a novel partial label dimensionality reduction method.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets are reported to validate improved generalization performance for different PLL algorithms.
SDLPP is reported to outperform state-of-the-art partial label dimensionality reduction methods.
The authors report that code is publicly accessible through the provided GitHub link.

narrative_sequence.summary: Partial label learning assigns each training example a candidate-label set containing one ground-truth label.
Existing methods overlook semantic dissimilarity relationships inferred from labeling confidences.
SDLPP combines semantic dissimilarity and local neighborhood information through alternating disambiguation, dissimilarity generation, and dimensionality reduction.
The method maps original data into a pre-specified low-dimensional feature space.
Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets are reported to show improved generalization and performance over existing methods.

source_observation.claim: The method uses labeling-confidence inner products to derive semantic dissimilarity and combines that relationship with local neighborhoods.

interpretation.claim: Weak supervision can provide relational signals beyond a single inferred label, and combining global and local structure may guide representation learning.

application.claim: For other weakly supervised dimensionality-reduction tasks, consider modeling confidence-derived pairwise relationships alongside neighborhood structure.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach transfers beyond partial label learning or which conditions are necessary for the confidence-based dissimilarity to be reliable.
